claims.claim: Deploy adapters communicate with the CLI using JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio (stdin/stdout)
Input is line-delimited JSON on stdin
Output is line-delimited JSON on stdout
Encoding is UTF-8
Max line size is 10 MB
Initial buffer is 64 KB
Each JSON-RPC message is a single line terminated by newline; the CLI sends requests and reads responses sequentially
Request envelope has jsonrpc "2.0", id, method and params fields
Success response carries jsonrpc, id and result
Error response carries jsonrpc, id and error with code and message
The protocol has a get_provider_info method
get_provider_info returns adapter metadata
get_provider_info request uses an empty params object
get_provider_info response example has result fields name, version, capabilities and config_schema
get_provider_info result field name is a string and required
get_provider_info result field version is a string and required
get_provider_info result field capabilities is a string array and optional
get_provider_info result field config_schema is an optional string holding a JSON Schema for config validation
The protocol has a validate_config method
validate_config validates provider configuration before planning
validate_config request uses a params object with a config string field holding JSON-encoded provider config
validate_config response example with valid true
validate_config invalid response example has valid false and an errors array
validate_config param config is a string holding JSON-encoded provider config
validate_config result field valid is a bool
validate_config result field errors is a string array
validate_config result field warnings is a string array
validate_config warnings are non-blocking and do not affect valid
The CLI prints validate_config warnings with a warning-sign prefix
The protocol has a plan method
plan analyzes the pack and config to determine which resources need to change
plan request params are pack_json, deploy_config, environment and prior_state
plan response example has result fields changes and summary, with change types agent_runtime and a2a_endpoint and actions CREATE and UPDATE
plan param pack_json is the serialized .pack.json contents
plan param deploy_config is a string holding the JSON-encoded merged provider config
plan param environment is a string holding the target environment name
plan param prior_state is opaque adapter state from prior deploy, empty on first deploy
plan result field changes is a ResourceChange array
plan result field summary is a human-readable string
plan result field warnings is a string array printed before the plan changes with a warning-sign prefix
ResourceChange has fields type, name, action and detail, all strings
ResourceChange action values are CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, DRIFT and NO_CHANGE
The protocol has an apply method
apply executes the deployment plan, creating, updating or deleting resources
apply request params are pack_json, deploy_config, environment and prior_state
apply response example has result fields adapter_state and events, with event types progress, resource and complete
apply params are pack_json, deploy_config, environment and prior_state (opaque, empty if first deploy), all strings
apply result field adapter_state is an opaque string the CLI persists
apply result field events is an ApplyEvent array
ApplyEvent type values are progress, resource, error and complete
ApplyEvent has message string and resource ResourceResult fields
ResourceResult status values are created, updated, deleted and failed
ResourceResult has fields type, name, action, status and detail, all strings
The protocol has a destroy method
destroy tears down all managed resources
destroy request params are deploy_config, environment and prior_state (no pack_json)
destroy response example has status destroyed and an events array with progress and complete events
destroy params are deploy_config, environment and prior_state, all strings
destroy result status is always destroyed on success
destroy result field events is a DestroyEvent array
The protocol has a status method
status queries current deployment status from the cloud provider
status request params are deploy_config, environment and prior_state
status response example has result fields status, resources and state
status params are deploy_config, environment and prior_state, all strings
status result field status values are deployed, not_deployed, degraded and unknown
status result field resources is a ResourceStatus array
status result field state is an optional string holding updated adapter state
ResourceStatus has fields type, name, status and detail, all strings
ResourceStatus status values are healthy, unhealthy and missing
The protocol has an import method
import imports a pre-existing resource into deployment state so the CLI can manage it
import request params are resource_type, resource_name, identifier, deploy_config, environment and prior_state
import response example has result fields resource and state
import param resource_type is a string such as agent_runtime
import param resource_name is the name assigned in local state
import param identifier is a provider-specific resource identifier string
import param prior_state is optional
import result field resource is a ResourceStatus
import result field state is the updated opaque adapter state string
The protocol has an optional get_login_url method
get_login_url is served only by adapters that advertise the login capability and implement the LoginProvider interface; other adapters return method-not-found
get_login_url returns the provider's browser authorize URL used by the deploy login command
The deploy login command exists
get_login_url request params are callback_url, state and config
get_login_url param callback_url is the CLI loopback callback the provider must redirect to
get_login_url param state is a CSRF nonce the provider must echo back
get_login_url param config is a JSON-encoded, possibly partial deploy config carrying provider coordinates such as api_endpoint
get_login_url result field authorize_url is the URL the CLI opens in the browser
The protocol has an optional complete_login method
complete_login is optional and exchanges the captured callback parameters for a deploy profile and a scoped token
complete_login request params are params (an object with code and state) and config
complete_login param params is an object of all query parameters captured from the loopback callback
complete_login param config is a JSON-encoded deploy config string
complete_login result field profile is an object holding endpoint, workspace, providers and skills to merge into the config
complete_login result field token is a string
The complete_login token is stored in the credentials file and never in the config
The protocol has an optional list_sessions method
list_sessions is served only by adapters that advertise the sessions capability and implement the SessionSourceProvider interface; other adapters return method-not-found
list_sessions is used by promptarena generate --source <adapter>
list_sessions request params are deploy_config, environment, filter_passed, expectations, limit and cursor
list_sessions param deploy_config is the merged deploy config (endpoint, workspace, api_token and profile fields), the same document plan and apply receive
list_sessions param environment is the deploy environment the config was merged for
list_sessions param filter_passed is an optional bool: true returns passed sessions only, false returns failed sessions only, absent returns all
list_sessions param filter_eval_type is an optional string filtering to sessions that recorded an eval of that type
list_sessions param expectations is an optional object array of {eval_id, min?, max?}
list_sessions param limit is an optional int page size where 0 means the adapter default
list_sessions param cursor is an optional string that continues a previous page
list_sessions result field sessions is an array of summaries with id, scenario_id, provider_id, timestamp, turn_count, has_failures, tags and metadata
list_sessions result field next_cursor is non-empty when more pages follow
Whether a filter is applied server-side is the adapter's choice
The CLI re-checks expectations against every session it fetches
A fetched session that violates no expectation is reported as skipped
The protocol has an optional get_session method
get_session is optional and returns one session in full
get_session request params are deploy_config, environment and session_id
get_session result session.messages is a JSON array of PromptKit types.Message with tool calls and results inline
get_session result session.pack is an optional object with name, version and digest
get_session result session.variables is an optional object of template variables
get_session result session.workflow is an optional object with entry_state, entry_prompt_task and transitions[{from, to, event, prompt_task, message_index}]
get_session result session.evals is an array of recorded evals with id, type, kind, score, passed, params, threshold, message, details and turn
Eval kind values are eval, assertion and guardrail
Redaction is the platform's responsibility and the adapter performs none
Error code -32700 is Parse Error
Error code -32600 is Invalid Request
Error code -32601 is Method Not Found
Error code -32603 is Internal Error for provider method errors
Adapters may return custom error codes with descriptive messages
Example adapter error response uses code -32603 with an AWS AccessDeniedException message
The CLI uses sequential integer request IDs starting from 1
The adapter must include the matching id in each response
Request IDs are not reused within a single session
The Adapter SDK page is a Go SDK for implementing this protocol
The Adapter Architecture page is at /arena/explanation/deploy/adapter-architecture/
The CLI Commands page is at /arena/reference/deploy/cli-commands/ and documents the CLI that drives the protocol
